standard_prerequisites.name: A finite locally free coherent module is reflexive
A coherent module whose stalks are free is finite locally free, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the converse to freeness of the stalk at each point.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local rings of dimension zero are fields and local rings of dimension one that are regular are discrete valuation rings, with torsion free finite modules over them free, cited from the algebra and more-algebra chapters
standard_prerequisites.use: Disposes of the points of dimension at most one.

standard_prerequisites.name: A reflexive module over a normal local ring has depth at least two, and a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module over a regular local ring is free, cited from the more-algebra and algebra chapters
standard_prerequisites.use: Disposes of the points of dimension two.

core_obligations: Easy direction and reduction: a finite locally free module is reflexive, and for the converse it suffices to show that the stalk of a reflexive coherent module is free at every point (proof lines 2347-2352).
Points of dimension zero: the local ring is a field and the stalk is free for trivial reasons (proof lines 2354-2355).

Points of dimension one: the regular local ring of dimension one is a discrete valuation ring, the stalk of a reflexive module is torsion free, and a finite torsion free module over a discrete valuation ring is free (proof lines 2356-2359).

Points of dimension two: the local ring is a regular local ring of dimension two, reflexivity forces depth at least two at that point, and a maximal Cohen-Macaulay finite module over a regular local ring is free (proof lines 2360-2367).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the converse to freeness of all stalks and check the three possible dimensions of a local ring separately, using the size of the local ring each time (proof lines 2347-2367).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that on a regular scheme of dimension at most two, a coherent module is reflexive if and only if it is finite locally free (statement lines 2336-2345). The counted proof is a short case analysis by the dimension of the local ring at a point: a field in dimension zero, a discrete valuation ring in dimension one where reflexivity gives torsion freeness and torsion free finite modules are free, and a regular local ring of dimension two where reflexivity gives depth at least two and a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module over a regular local ring is free (proof lines 2347-2367). It is H2: the reduction and all three cases are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard facts about local rings of small dimension.
